result.note: Tested the US waiver that enabled India's first Iranian oil import since 2019, the buyer and the destination coast. Skipped the year India stopped buying, because the story gives both 2019 and 'five years ago'.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, India was set to receive its first Iranian oil shipment since 2019. Consider the following statements about this shipment:
items: It followed a 30-day US waiver allowing countries to buy Iranian oil already at sea.
The cargo was bought by a privately owned Indian refiner.
The tanker carrying the cargo was heading to India's west coast.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Only the first statement is correct. The state-run Indian Oil Corp bought the cargo aboard the VLCC Jaya, which was originally headed for China and is now heading to India's east coast. The waiver covered roughly 170 million barrels loaded by March 20 and discharged by April 19.
questions.source: State-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC) snagged the cargo aboard the VLCC Jaya, which was originally headed for China and is currently heading to India’s east coast.
